title: Spatial transcriptomics of the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans using RNA tomography
author: Schild, Mars, et al.

steps.title: Add Trizol‑ERCC mixture
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL Trizol mixed with 0.1 µL ERCC spike‑ins (diluted 1:500 000 in nuclease‑free water) to each 0.5 mL microcentrifuge tube that contains a frozen tissue slice; shake vigorously for 5 s.

steps.title: Phase separation with chloroform
steps.instruction: Spin the tubes at 12 000 g, 4 °C for a few seconds; add 20 µL chloroform to each tube, shake vigorously for 5 s; spin again at 12 000 g, 4 °C for 15 min.

steps.title: Precipitate RNA with isopropanol and Glycoblue
steps.instruction: Number the tubes, add 0.2 µL Glycoblue (15 mg/mL) to each; transfer ~60 µL of the upper aqueous phase to the numbered tube, add 60 µL isopropanol and shake vigorously for 5 s.

steps.title: Store RNA precipitate
steps.instruction: Pause point – store the tubes at –20 °C for at least 48 h (longer storage increases final RNA yield).

steps.title: Pellet RNA and ethanol washes
steps.instruction: Spin at 12 000 g, 4 °C for 18 min; carefully aspirate supernatant with a small‑tip pipette; add 180 µL freshly diluted 75 % ethanol (20‑25 °C), vortex, spin at 7 500 g, 4 °C for 10 min; repeat the ethanol wash once more; aspirate supernatant and remove residual ethanol droplets with a 2 µL pipette.

steps.title: Air‑dry RNA pellet
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the pellet until completely dry, but for no more than 10 min (optimal drying ~6–7 min); avoid over‑drying to prevent RNA degradation.

steps.title: Warm AMPure XP beads
steps.instruction: Allow AMPure XP beads to equilibrate to room temperature (20‑25 °C).

steps.title: Pool cDNA reactions
steps.instruction: Pool all cDNA reactions belonging to the same animal into one tube; spin down pooled reactions for 1 min at 12 000 g and transfer the lower aqueous phase to a new microcentrifuge tube. If >35 sections are used, split the pool into multiple 1.5 mL tubes.

steps.title: Prepare bead‑binding mix
steps.instruction: Prepare a bead mix at a 1:7 ratio of AMPure XP beads to bead‑binding buffer; vortex well; add the mix to the cDNA sample at a 4:5 ratio (e.g., 80 µL bead mix for 100 µL cDNA).

steps.title: Bind cDNA to beads
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture at room temperature (20‑25 °C) for 15 min.

steps.title: Capture beads on magnetic stand
steps.instruction: Place the tube on a magnetic stand for at least 5 min until the liquid is clear.

steps.title: Wash beads with 80 % ethanol (first)
steps.instruction: Remove and discard the supernatant; add 800 µL fresh 80 % ethanol, incubate minimally (≈30 s), then discard the ethanol without disturbing the beads.

steps.title: Wash beads with 80 % ethanol (second)
steps.instruction: Repeat the ethanol wash; after the second wash, remove all supernatant without disturbing the beads.

steps.title: Air‑dry beads
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the beads for approximately 6–7 min (maximum 10 min) to avoid over‑drying caused by residual mineral oil.

steps.title: Elute purified cDNA
steps.instruction: Resuspend the beads in 8 µL nuclease‑free water; pipette up‑and‑down 10 times; incubate at room temperature (20‑25 °C) for 2 min; place on magnetic stand until liquid is clear; transfer the entire supernatant to a new 0.5 mL tube.

steps.title: Store purified cDNA
steps.instruction: Pause point – store the 8 µL cDNA at –20 °C for up to one week before proceeding to library preparation.

steps.title: Prime aRNA for reverse transcription
steps.instruction: To 5 µL aRNA, add 1 µL random hexamer RT primers (20 µM) and 0.5 µL dNTPs (10 µM); incubate at 65 °C for 5 min, then place on ice.

steps.title: First‑strand synthesis master mix
steps.instruction: Prepare a master mix (room temperature, 20‑25 °C) containing: 2.0 µL 2× First Strand Buffer, 1.0 µL 0.1 M DTT, 0.5 µL RNase Inhibitor (40 U/µL), 0.5 µL SuperScript II (200 U/µL). Add 4 µL of this mix to the primed aRNA; incubate 10 min at 25 °C then 1 h at 42 °C (thermal cycler lid set to 50 °C or hybridization oven).

steps.title: Prepare PCR amplification mix
steps.instruction: Prepare a 40 µL master mix per sample containing: 11 µL nuclease‑free water, 25 µL 2× High‑fidelity PCR master mix, 2 µL RNA PCR primer (RP1), 2 µL unique index RNA PCR primer (RPIX). Ensure each sample receives a uniquely indexed RPIX primer.

steps.title: Amplify cDNA by PCR
steps.instruction: Add the 40 µL PCR mix to each 8 µL cDNA; run the following program: 30 s at 98 °C; 11 cycles of 10 s at 98 °C, 30 s at 60 °C, 30 s at 72 °C; final extension 10 min at 72 °C; hold at 4 °C. If aRNA is low, increase to up to 15 cycles.

steps.title: Pause after PCR
steps.instruction: Pause point – samples may be stored at –20 °C for up to one week.

steps.title: First AMPure bead cleanup of PCR product
steps.instruction: Warm AMPure XP beads to room temperature, vortex; add beads at a 1:1 ratio to the PCR reaction (50 µL beads for a 50 µL reaction, or 25 µL beads if the reaction was halved); mix by pipetting up‑and‑down ten times.

steps.title: Bind and wash beads (first cleanup)
steps.instruction: Incubate 15 min at room temperature; place on magnetic stand ≥5 min until liquid is clear; remove and discard 95 µL (or 45 µL for a 25 µL reaction) supernatant; add 200 µL fresh 80 % ethanol, incubate ≥30 s, discard supernatant without disturbing beads; repeat the ethanol wash; air‑dry beads for 15 min or until completely dry.

steps.title: Elute PCR product from beads
steps.instruction: Resuspend beads in 25 µL nuclease‑free water; pipette up‑and‑down ten times; incubate 2 min at room temperature; place on magnetic stand for 5 min; transfer the 25 µL supernatant to a new microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Second AMPure bead cleanup
steps.instruction: Add 25 µL AMPure XP beads (1:1 ratio) to the 25 µL eluate; mix, incubate 15 min at room temperature, magnet for ≥5 min; wash twice with 200 µL 80 % ethanol as before; air‑dry beads for 15 min; resuspend in 10 µL nuclease‑free water; incubate 2 min, magnet 5 min; transfer the 10 µL supernatant (DNA library) to a new tube.

steps.title: Quantify DNA library
steps.instruction: Measure library concentration using Qubit (use 1 µL of the sample); expected concentration ≥1 ng/µL.

steps.title: Assess library size distribution
steps.instruction: Run 1 µL of the library on a Bioanalyzer with a high‑sensitivity DNA chip; expected size distribution peak between 200 bp and 1000 bp.

description: Note: We provide two different protocols, one with RNA isolation (protocol A) and one without (protocol B). In our experience, both approaches can produce high-quality libraries for sequencing, but there are some limitations that should be considered before starting the procedure. By first isolating the RNA, the input material will be more pure and smaller volumes of reagents can be used. However, the manual processing of large numbers of samples is labor intensive and may increase the chance of RNA degradation. Without RNA isolation, the hands-on time is much shorter, but the quality of the input material will be lower. For clarity, the parts of the method that are different between protocol A and B are described separately.Note: We recommend first testing the protocol with control RNA. There are several options available, such as HeLa-S3 RNA (Ambion).
